<!--
NUMBER PENDING, as for the other rebuilt supplements. Replaces the draft
`figure_4_supplement_residuals.Rmd` of 2026-07-31, which paired the residual's memory with its
variance; the variance is recorded at the foot of this note and is one side away from being drawn
again.

WHAT IT IS, as drawn since 2026-08-12: ONE panel over the plane, all eight members, one column
each. The note below was written for the two-panel version and is kept because the removed side is
still described in it; what the file renders is side A alone (see the sides chunk).

  A  tau_int   the integrated autocorrelation of the standardized residual (patch - y_mean) /
               sqrt(y_var), in normalized Sokal / Kish form. Null 1 for a white residual. It counts
               how many intervals the likelihood effectively has for every interval it believes it
               has, and it is computed from the DATA against the fitted mean and variance, with no
               parameter, no derivative and no likelihood comparison.
  B  kappa     the condition number of the Gaussian Fisher: lambda_max / lambda_min. Null 1 for a
               design that determines every direction equally. It says whether the experiment
               PINS the parameters at all, which is a different question from whether the error
               bar is honest.

They are together because they are the two questions a reader asks that Figure 4 does not answer,
and because both are scalars per cell with no parameter index, so each costs one column per member
and the two of them fill the width at a 1.38 mm cell — wider than the body figure's 1.14.

TWO BARS, NOT ONE, and this is the first figure in the set to need it. Everywhere else the
quantities are commensurable and share the scale by construction, which is what makes a colour mean
one thing across the whole set. Here they are not: tau_int runs from 1.00 to 9.3 and kappa from
360 to 4.9e7. On one scale the finer of the two would sit inside a single band in every cell. So
side A takes the one-sided sequential scale with the set's own criteria, 1.15 and 2, which here
read as "the likelihood is over-counting its data by 15 per cent" and "by a factor two"; side B
takes decade bands with the one mark it has, 3e4, which is the ill-conditioning threshold this
project already used when the maps still greyed cells out. Neither borrows the other's colours and
neither borrows the diverging scale's, so nothing on this page can be confused with a distortion.

WHAT IT SHOWS. Medians over the seven intervals at noise 0.1, re-measured 2026-08-12 with the
un-averaged arm on the roster. THE ROW THIS NOTE USED TO CALL "LSE" IS ILSE: the table was written
against the data key `nonlinearsqr`, which is the av = 1 arm, and the label was corrected across
the set on 2026-08-06. The genuinely un-averaged arm is the new first row of each block.

                  N_ch:      10       100      1000     10000
    tau_int       LSE      8.612    9.144    9.269    9.246
                  ILSE     8.684    9.233    9.325    9.286
                  NR       7.856    8.611    3.010    1.337
                  INR      8.170    9.051    9.160    9.199
                  R        1.140    1.284    1.346    1.373
                  MR       1.308    1.633    1.773    1.816
                  VR       1.218    1.455    1.515    1.536
                  IR       1.038    1.011    1.001    1.005
    kappa         LSE      722      5.18e3   4.86e5   4.69e7
                  ILSE     709      5.30e3   5.29e5   4.88e7
                  NR       738      1312     1.59e4   7.06e5
                  INR      647      1203     1.13e4   1.13e5
                  R        537      417      1451     1.49e4
                  MR       454      413      2172     2.22e4
                  VR       414      359      1786     1.82e4
                  IR       434      373      985      1.01e4

The two least-squares arms are within a per cent of each other in both quantities at this noise
level, which is what makes the eighth column a completeness matter rather than a new reading: it is
there so a reader fitting the un-averaged classical model can find their own panel. Over the whole
plane the two part at the coarsest sampling, the worst cell being N_ch 1e4 at Delta_tilde = 1,
where ILSE's tau_int is 1.81 and LSE's 2.48.

PANEL A IS THE DEGREES-OF-FREEDOM ARGUMENT, in the data. Least squares and the two open-loop
members leave about nine intervals of memory for every interval they count, so they behave as
though they had nine times more independent observations than the recording supplies; the
recursive filter leaves 1.3, the one-endpoint pair 1.5 to 1.8, and the boundary-conditioned filter
1.00. That ordering is the same one every likelihood-level figure reports, obtained without any of
the likelihood-level machinery, which is why this panel is worth its width.

READ NR WITH CARE, and the caption must say so. Its memory FALLS with the channel count, to 1.34
at ten thousand, which alone would read as a residual gone white and a likelihood gone honest. It
has not: NR's predicted variance is 29.6 times too large there (see the foot of this note), and an
inflated denominator whitens a normalized residual whatever structure it had. The two panels of
this figure do not catch that; the r^2/n side does, which is the argument for restoring it.

PANEL B IS NOT A RESTATEMENT OF PANEL A, and the numbers show it. The condition number grows with
the channel count for every member, but it separates them by four orders of magnitude at ten
thousand channels: 4.9e7 for least squares against 1.0e4 for the boundary-conditioned filter, with
the rest ordered in between exactly as the cost ladder is. So the members that condition better
also leave a better-posed problem, which is a claim about the DESIGN and not about calibration.
It has to be read as a separate reading and not as a mask: over the shared grid the condition
number and the distortion are close to orthogonal (Spearman 0.25 overall, and NEGATIVE for IR, for
which worse conditioning goes with better calibration). Cells exist that are well-conditioned and
miscalibrated, and cells exist that are ill-posed and perfectly honest.

THE THIRD SIDE, one line away. r^2/n, the mean squared standardized residual over the number of
intervals the recording holds, null 1: it is 1.000 for LSE, INR, R and IR at every channel count
and 3.710 and 29.643 for NR at a thousand and ten thousand. That is the same divergence its
per-sample distortion shows (47) and its analytic-against-numerical Fisher shows (0.55), visible
in the raw data. Two cautions travel with it: r2_std is emitted as the SUM over the recording's
intervals, so the divisor is the NUMBER OF INTERVALS, 10 / interval_in_tau, and not the emitted
`count`, which is 10000 and is the number of simulations; and the LSE 1.000 is a TAUTOLOGY, since
the classical fit marginalises its noise scale and standardizes the residual by a variance fitted
to that very residual.

MR, VR AND INR WERE SHORT COLUMNS when this was written (three, two and one noise level, so grey
above and tiles rather than contours below MIN_CONTOUR_LEVELS). They are not any more: measured
2026-08-12 off figures/figure_4_source_data/figure_4_source_data_cell_scalars.csv, every member
of the roster carries 210 cells, thirty (N_ch, noise) combinations by seven sampling intervals,
and IR carries 294. The grid is auto-detected per knit, so that filled in with no edit here,
exactly as the note promised.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
# ALL EIGHT since 2026-08-12: neither quantity needs a parameter, so every member costs one column.
# The eighth is the un-averaged least-squares arm, and it is the one column of this map a reader is
# most likely to be standing in: the classical fit an experimentalist has already run is more often
# least squares on the sample than on the interval average, and this figure exists to let them place
# their own recording. It carries the same 210 cells as every other member (figures/data/a202e03).
FIG4_ALGOS     <- c("nonlinearsqr_g", "nonlinearsqr", "macro_NR", "macro_INR", "macro_R",
                    "macro_MR", "macro_VR", "macro_IR")
FIG4_ALGO_LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr_g = "LSE", nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_NR = "NR",
                    macro_INR = "INR", macro_R = "R",
                    macro_MR = "MR", macro_VR = "VR", macro_IR = "IR")
# a202e03 is where the un-averaged arm lives, and it has to be on the search path for a second
# reason as well: the shared source CSVs are stamped by the COUNT of input files
# (figure_4_data.R:245), so a notebook that cannot see that directory rebuilds them without that
# arm and every other figure then loses a column. That is how this file lost it in the first place.
FIG4_DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b",
                    "../data/a202e03")
# The inner level is the QUANTITY. Each side's data carries only its own, so each member gets one
# column per side and the strip names what is in it.
FIG4_PARS   <- c("lag", "kappa")
FIG4_PSHORT <- c(lag = "tau[int]", kappa = "kappa")
source("figure_4_common.R")
source("figure_4_layout.R")
```

```{r sides}
# Both quantities come out of the shared source data (figure_4_data.R), which swept them in the
# same pass as everything else, so this notebook reads three small CSVs and no battery file.
lk <- dplyr::filter(.fig4_src$scal, algo %in% ALGOS, param %in% c("lag", "kappa"),
                    is.finite(v), v > 0)

# SIDE B REMOVED 2026-08-12 (Luciano). The condition number left this file with the pairing that
# built it. Two reasons, and the second is the decisive one. tau_int runs 1.00 to 9.3 and kappa
# runs over decades, so they cannot share a bar, and this was the only page in the set needing two
# -- a colour stopped meaning one thing. And kappa has no citing sentence anywhere: its whole job
# in the paper is the masking rule kappa > 3e4, which Methods states in prose and needs no map.
# The remaining side is the one an experimentalist can compute on their own recording, which is
# what makes this a Figure 5 supplement and not a Figure 4 one.
SIDES <- list(
  list(lab = "memory left in the standardized residual", letter = "A",
       data = dplyr::filter(lk, param == "lag"), zf = function(x) log10(x$v),
       scale = modifyList(SCALE_ONESIDED,
                          list(title = "intervals per interval,\nas a factor"))))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 6.85}
# 8 columns over ONE side, no key row and no white contours: a standard error is not defined for a
# quantity with no parameter. Dropping side B roughly doubles the cell width at a fixed 7.4 in, so
# the old two-side knob 0.2126 leaves the render half as tall as it should be. The seven-column
# render was 0.4624; the eighth column narrows the cell by a factor 7/8, so the first guess was
# 0.4624 x 7/8 = 0.4046, corrected by one measured pass to the value below.
# Verify with `python3 tmp/measure_fig4.py <pdf>` against 100 per cent.
fig4_render(SIDES, per_row = 0.4005, out = "Figure_5_S3.pdf",
            se_lines = FALSE, key = FALSE)
```
